title: Spectrum, semimodules and projectives of the inverse semiring $R_0$ of Faul, Goswami, Joubert and Manuell
subject: math.RA
abstract: Faul, Goswami, Joubert and Manuell made the case for inverse semirings, the semirings whose additive monoid is an inverse monoid. One of their basic examples is the semiring $R_0$ obtained from a ring $R$ by adjoining a new zero; they showed that $\mathbb Z_0$ is the initial inverse semiring and that every module over an inverse semiring has an inverse additive monoid. Caviglia, Faul, Manuell and Mesiti then described every inverse semiring by an idempotent semiring and a lax monoidal functor from it to abelian groups; for $R_0$ the idempotent semiring is the Boolean semifield. For a nonzero commutative ring $R$ we determine the prime spectrum of $R_0$, its congruences, its semimodules and its finitely generated projective semimodules. The spectrum is $\operatorname{Spec} R$ with one new point below all others, at which the localization is the Boolean semifield. The semimodules are the strong semilattices of $R$-modules: families of $R$-modules indexed by a join-semilattice, with linear maps along the order; this is the counterpart for semimodules of the description of Caviglia, Faul, Manuell and Mesiti. The finitely generated projective ones are classified by finite posets carrying a finitely generated projective $R$-module at each element, and their semilattices of idempotents are exactly the finite distributive lattices. Since the $\mathbb Z_0$-semimodules are the commutative inverse monoids, the case $R=\mathbb Z$ is Clifford's theorem together with a classification of the finitely generated projective commutative inverse monoids. Finally, $R\mapsto R_0$ is fully faithful on commutative rings, and when the units of $R$ have no common nonzero fixed point, the two zeros of $R_0$ are exactly the common fixed points of the units. The construction began as an idea of the depositor's, in a conversation with Gemini 2.5 Pro (Gemini app). The results were produced by Gemini 2.5 Deep Think (Gemini app, Deep Think mode) and by GPT-5-series Pro models (ChatGPT Pro mode, at reasoning effort ultra), checked and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, and checked again and edited by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked the proofs.
comments: The semiring $R_0$ is Definition 3.6 of Faul, Goswami, Joubert and Manuell, The case for inverse semirings, arXiv:2411.12318 (2024), which came first; that $\mathbb Z_0$ is the initial inverse semiring and that modules over inverse semirings have inverse additive monoids are theirs (Propositions 5.1 and 6.1). Caviglia, Faul, Manuell and Mesiti, arXiv:2607.12944, Theorem 8.5, describe inverse semirings as lax monoidal functors from idempotent semirings to abelian groups; Theorem 2 here is the corresponding statement for semimodules over $R_0$. The description of commutative inverse monoids as strong semilattices of groups is Clifford's (1941); projective semilattices are Horn and Kimura's (1971) and projective distributive lattices Balbes and Horn's (1970). How it was produced. The construction began as an idea of the depositor's, in a conversation with Gemini 2.5 Pro (Google, Gemini app), and was formalized in November 2025 by Gemini 2.5 Deep Think (Gemini app, Deep Think mode). In March 2026 a GPT-5-series Pro model (OpenAI) in ChatGPT Pro mode, at reasoning effort ultra, extracted the usable part of that work, and GPT-5-series Pro models in ChatGPT Pro mode, at reasoning effort ultra, produced the statements and first proofs of Theorems 2 and 3. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max checked every proof, with exact computations, wrote out the proof of Theorem 3 and the classification of congruences, proved the results of Section 6 in the generality given, and wrote the first version of the text (21-23 November 2026). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) at effort max followed every proof again, repaired one step, added Corollary 4, Proposition 5.3, Remarks 3.3 and 4.2 with proofs, and edited the text (23 November 2026). Before deposit, GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode) found two sentences of the draft false in a later research run; Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max confirmed this, and Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max corrected them and proved the corrected statement (Remark 5.4), 24 November 2026. None of this work knew of the paper of Faul, Goswami, Joubert and Manuell, which came first. No human has checked the proofs.
